idea: How to prevent bathroom pipe problems
title: Preventing Bathroom Blockages at the P-Trap
description: Educational guide on how bathroom P-traps collect debris and how maintaining them prevents deep drain line blockages.
image_prompt: A detailed, professional educational technical cutaway photograph of a white PVC P-trap assembly beneath a clean bathroom vanity sink, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The image clearly demonstrates a cross-section of the trap bend: standing water forms a proper water seal inside the curve, while visual organic debris such as hair and soap film rests concentrated at the lowest point of the U-bend. Clean interior, realistic pipe thickness, threaded slip nuts, wall arm extension, realistic pipe geometry and water physics. Professional natural indoor lighting, crisp focus on the cutaway section, shallow depth of field highlighting the fitting. Clean plumber work area environment. No text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no diagrams, no extra overlay graphics.
visual_story: The visual shows a clear cross-sectional cutaway of a standard PVC P-trap under a bathroom sink. It highlights where hair and soap scum accumulate at the lowest point of the trap bend while water maintains the seal. This visual illustrates that the trap is designed to catch debris early before it reaches unexposed wall piping, teaching viewers the physical mechanism of drain restriction.

on_image_text.hook: Stop Bathroom Clogs Before They Reach Your Main Line
on_image_text.explanation: Hair and soap scum settle at the bottom bend of the P-trap, restricting water flow over time.
on_image_text.takeaway: Clean the removable trap bend regularly to protect branch drainage pipes.
